answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:150-157 holds mi_rank, which does the grade mapping: chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0)). At score 9 both terms are true, giving 67 ('C'). At 10 and 19 only the second term is true, giving 66 ('B'). At 20 neither is true, giving 65 ('A'). This matches the docstring: A above 19, B for 9<s<=19, C at 9 or below. The boundaries are inclusive on the lower grade, and the bool-arithmetic expression is easy to misread. The review should confirm the boundary values 9, 10, 19 and 20 against the existing parametrized MI_RANK_CASES test in radon/tests/test_other_metrics.py. Time on radon/raw.py and radon/visitors.py covers the inputs to the score: raw.py supplies the LOC and comment counts used by the maintainability index calculation, and visitors.py supplies the complexity and Halstead figures. Checking them confirms that nothing upstream shifts a score across a threshold through rounding or clamping. radon/complexity.py only ranks cyclomatic complexity, so it gets a brief check to make sure its letter grading is not confused with the MI ranking.
